english: Let $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $F(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{x}(t-3)\,|t-2|\,dt$. Then the minimum value of $F$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $F(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{x}(t-3)\,|t-2|\,dt$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $F$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: $F'<0$ on $(-\infty,2)$ and $(2,3)$ (no sign change at $2$), $F'>0$ on $(3,\infty)$: $F$ decreases up to $3$, then increases, so the minimum is $F(3)$
solution_full: Critical points: $x=2$ and $x=3$. For $x<3$, $x\neq2$: $x-3<0$ and $|x-2|>0$, so $F'<0$; for $x>3$, $F'>0$. Thus $F$ is decreasing on $(-\infty,3]$ (the point $2$ is stationary but not an extremum) and increasing on $[3,\infty)$, and $F(3)$ is the minimum value.
originality_note: New: the integrand has a stationary point without sign change (the modulus factor) and the global minimum is at the other root, where the integral must be split at the corner (way 5). Closest known: minimum of int_0^x (t-a)(t-b) dt. Different because: the modulus produces a double-root-like point that is not an extremum, and the lower limit -2 makes the value non-trivial.
blueprint_concepts: Maxima and minima of a function defined by a definite integral

concept_use.Maxima and minima of a function defined: F' = (x-3)|x-2| changes sign only at x = 3; x = 2 is stationary without an extremum, so F(3) is the minimum, evaluated by splitting at t = 2.

stem_review: Read as a student: F has domain/codomain; the minimum exists (F decreasing then increasing, F -> infinity). Checked with sympy: -59/2. Answer -29.50, a negative decimal as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Sign of F' = (x-3)|x-2| shows the minimum is at x = 3; split the integral at t = 2.
justification: Routine chain: derivative of an integral function, sign analysis, one split integral. Lighter than 2023-P2-Q8 (L3); L2.
